chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhūr, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthmān, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“Those who say: Our Lord is Allah, then remain steadfast.”
So Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام said: “They remained steadfast upon the Imams, one after another.”
“The angels descend upon them: Do not fear, nor grieve, and receive glad tidings of the Paradise which you were promised.”

key_terms.اسْتَقَامُوا: they remained steadfast; here, they remained firm in adherence
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams; the divinely appointed leaders to whom steadfastness is directed
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, promised to those who remain steadfast
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who bring reassurance and glad tidings
key_terms.تَتَنَزَّلُ: they descend repeatedly; describing the descent of the angels
key_terms.تُوعَدُونَ: you were promised; indicating the divine promise of reward

ai.seo_question: What does “then remain steadfast” mean in Shia tafsir of Qur'an 41:30?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic description of steadfastness as steadfastness upon the Imams, one after another. It presents wilayah and continuity in obedience to the divinely appointed Imams as the meaning of istiqamah in this verse, along with the promise of angelic reassurance and Paradise.
